texts: A retrograde type A dissection two days after TEVAR is a surgical emergency, best treated by replacing the ascending aorta and the whole arch, joined directly to the stent graft.
The new tear usually starts at the proximal end of the stent graft and climbs back into the ascending aorta.
Only a total arch replacement reaches down to the stent graft and removes the entry tear; a hemi-arch leaves torn arch between the new graft and the stent graft.
More TEVAR further up does not treat an ascending dissection, and medical therapy alone carries a high risk of rupture and tamponade.
In the picture, Franky sews a new white arch and rising neck straight onto the top of the silver sleeve and cuts the backward zipper out.
Memory hook: when the zipper climbs back from the sleeve, sew white all the way down to the silver.
